title: Quadrilaterals and Polygons: Properties and Angle Sums
seo_title: Grade 8 Quadrilaterals and Polygons Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Explore properties of the sides, angles and diagonals of quadrilaterals (parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezium, kite); solve geometric problems involving unknown sides and angles in quadrilaterals using known properties.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 quadrilaterals worksheets: angles in quadrilaterals, properties and diagonals, polygon angle sums and regular polygons. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
  • A parallelogram has opposite sides and angles equal; a rectangle has equal diagonals; a rhombus has perpendicular diagonals.
  • The angles of an n-sided polygon add up to (n − 2) × 180°.
  • Each angle of a regular polygon = (n − 2) × 180° ÷ n.

Examples

Example

A regular hexagon

(6 − 2) × 180 = 720

Answer: each angle 120°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
180° in a quadrilateralA quadrilateral is 360°.
All diagonals equalOnly in rectangles and squares.
n × 180°Use (n − 2) × 180°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 118°, 97° and 95°. What is the fourth angle?
In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 48°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 48° = 132°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 88°, 77° and 89°. What is the fourth angle?
In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 65°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 65° = 115°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 61°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 61° = 119°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 94°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 94° = 86°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 124°. What is angle C?
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal: 124°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 103°. What is angle C?
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal: 103°.

items.q: An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 80° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 80° = 100°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 84°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 84° = 96°.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 4x + 4 and MR = x + 13. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 4x + 4 = x + 13. So 3x = 9 and x = 3.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 30 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 8 cm and 15 cm. Side = √(8² + 15²) = 17 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 44 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 44 = 22 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 5 cm and 12 cm. Side = √(5² + 12²) = 13 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 2x + 4 and MR = x + 7. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 2x + 4 = x + 7. So x = 3 and x = 3.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 3x + 1 and BD = 10 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 3x + 1 = 10, so 3x = 9 and x = 3.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 26 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 26 = 13 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 50 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 50 = 25 cm.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 2x + 3 and BD = 21 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 2x + 3 = 21, so 2x = 18 and x = 9.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 3x + 5 and MR = x + 13. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 3x + 5 = x + 13. So 2x = 8 and x = 4.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rectangle. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length and cut each other in half. They do not cross at right angles unless the rectangle is a square.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are equal, cross at right angles and cut each other in half?
items.e: Equal diagonals come from being a rectangle, and right angles where they cross come from being a rhombus. Only a square is both.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Its diagonals meet at E. What is the size of angle AEB?
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles, so angle AEB = 90°. (60° and 120° are angles of the rhombus itself.)

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rhombus. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles and cut each other in half. They are not equal: one is long and one is short.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Its diagonals meet at E. AE = 6 cm. How long is AC?
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram cut each other in half, so E is the middle of AC. AC = 6 + 6 = 12 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral cut each other in half. They are not equal and not at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Diagonals that cut each other in half make a parallelogram. Not equal: not a rectangle. Not at right angles: not a rhombus.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this parallelogram. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: In every parallelogram the diagonals cut each other in half. In this one they are not equal and do not cross at right angles.

items.q: ABCD is a square. Its diagonals meet at E. AC = 12 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a square are equal and cut each other in half. BD = 12 cm, so BE = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rhombus. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
They are not equal in length
They do not cross at right angles
items.e: The diagonals of this rhombus are different lengths. They do cross at right angles and cut each other in half. Only a square has equal diagonals among rhombuses.

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral are equal and cut each other in half, but they do not cross at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Diagonals that cut each other in half make a parallelogram. Equal diagonals make it a rectangle. Not at right angles, so not a square.

items.e: A rectangle only needs 4 right angles, and every square has them. The other statements are only sometimes true.

items.q: The short stick of Ravi’s kite is 60 cm long, and the long stick crosses it at its middle. How far is the crossing point from each end of the short stick?
items.e: The long diagonal cuts the short one in half: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm.

items.q: Ethan measures a quadrilateral’s diagonals. Both are 10 cm, and they cut each other in half at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Equal diagonals that cut each other in half: rectangle. At right angles too: rhombus. Both: a square.

items.q: Lerato draws a quadrilateral. All 4 sides are 5 cm. Its diagonals are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. The diagonals are different lengths, so it is not a square. (Half-diagonals 3 cm and 4 cm make 5 cm sides.)

items.q: Liam’s dad builds a deck frame. Opposite sides are 4 m and 3 m, so it is a parallelogram. He measures both diagonals: 5 m and 5 m. What does this tell him?
items.e: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle, so all 4 corners are right angles. Builders check corners this way.

items.q: Sarah covers a bulletin board with congruent parallelogram tiles. One tile has sides of 4 cm and 7 cm. What is the perimeter of each tile?
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal: 4 + 7 + 4 + 7 = 22 cm. (28 is 4 × 7, not a perimeter.)

items.q: Dumisani makes a stained-glass design from 4 congruent kites placed around a centre point, each one a quarter turn from the next. What is the order of rotational symmetry of the design?
items.e: Each quarter turn moves every kite onto the next one, so the design fits onto itself 4 times in a full turn: order 4.

items.q: Sarah paints a sign shaped like a parallelogram. One angle is 70°. What is the size of an angle next to it?
items.e: Angles next to each other in a parallelogram add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°. The angle opposite the 70° angle is also 70°.

items.q: Priya sews 8 congruent rhombus patches for a quilt. Each side of one patch is 6 cm. How much ribbon does she need to go around all 8 patches?
items.e: One patch: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. The patches are congruent, so 8 patches need 8 × 24 = 192 cm.

items.q: Andile cuts a rectangular piece of cardboard, 30 cm by 20 cm, along one diagonal. What is true about the two pieces?
items.e: A diagonal cuts a rectangle into 2 triangles with sides 30 cm, 20 cm and the diagonal. A half turn puts one exactly on the other, so they are congruent.
